controlled_experiment.method: Private native EKV and DurableServer stores, four schedulers. Suspend one data writer, issue one heartbeat-backend put to the shared store and one to a separate heartbeat store, verify independent completion, resume writer, verify both writes succeed. No preview store modifications. This is a blocking-path experiment, not a replay of the actual failure.

store_after_failure.note: Deletion tombstones and CAS metadata are not running agents. Counts taken after recovery; they do not establish the writer operation in progress at failure.

conclusion: The node lost its liveness deadline while heartbeat writes shared the agent-data writer path. A slow successful write consumed part of the next heartbeat budget. The watchdog killed the lifecycle manager; the supervisor uses one_for_all, interrupting the agent tree and causing placement failures.
remaining_uncertainty: No per-writer queue, current-operation, scheduler-latency or disk-latency samples were retained for the failed interval. The exact cause of the later stalled write (queueing, GC, disk or scheduling) cannot be established retrospectively.
recommended_change: Use native DurableServer heartbeat_backend with a separately supervised/managed EKV store so agent snapshot/cleanup queues cannot block node heartbeats. Keep the safety watchdog. Measure native heartbeat age and put duration alongside writer queue and scheduler latency in the next scale replay.
